inventions: NALŪN: Hall of Links (the dome in his art); call-towers (the minaret-like towers, used by criers); the unfinished triumphal arch in his art explained as Marshal Han Do-yun's, raised when Sum-gol was still the whole South, paid in bills that went dead after his quartermaster stopped a drain, and now entered as a forfeit with interest running.

NALŪN: the march contract (road, term, bread schedule, token for the marshal; looting kills his war-chest paper) and the quiet fee paid to each side, which is how the cities pay both sides and owe neither.

NALŪN: 'surety', 'the call' and 'reading a man's seal' as the local words for coat, Pressure and sensing; amber Chain Guard surcoats; Bridgemarch's council platform slung over the drop; odds posted on the Trial of Ten Deals; jokes such as 'paid in full', the cheese-board face and 'conquered eleven times and billed for it twelve'.

CHARTER: the opening case of 677 IC: Whitlow Sixtoes (Catkin wax-carrier), clerk Corbin Ashlar, Examiner Dame Isolde Averell, the refund of six copper, the riot with forty-one dead, and the phrase 'a Sealhall refund'.

CHARTER: the window instruction that writes an unpapered petitioner as 'nemo', nobody. This is offered as the origin of the Russet Crown's 'nobody' on the rolls. Brokencollar is only said to claim Whitlow reached it.

CHARTER: the Crown in Charter (the Concord's composite crown, pledged to the chancery after the Great Concord Splintering, and the Sealed Charter as the instrument that did it); the bill of sale 'one carcass, condition as seen', bought from a bankrupt town council; the First Beam; Long Spine Street; the Witnesses, called Cory and Tess; the Hall of the Seal; the Founders' Yard.

CHARTER: Waxgate's trade (hives, verdigris green, smalt blue, gold leaf, the Worshipful Company of Waxmakers, the hand-dab gate toll, the unnamed obsidian shed); the Marrowkin assessor who visits every ten years; the Legion drilling below the walls in blue and white.

MIDMARCH: nearly everything, since nothing was on file: the river Aldwater; the Tuppence kings (Gerent III) and the 662 IC fight on the bridge with Marrick captain Sella Drax; the Standing Army of about two hundred that marches the kingdom each morning; the Scale Minster (the green-roofed cathedral in his art, made a Sancta Lux house).

MIDMARCH: Queen Tizz Copperwick IV of Tollgarth and the Self-Minding Portcullis; the Harl Hills; King Ambrose Fivefold and the Stitch Hills; Crown Row; the coronation law of three neighboring crowns, or two and a Measurewright; the Coat-Turning fair every tenth summer.

MIDMARCH: the Guild counts of 83 and 117 crowns; the sects Sixth Arch Boys and Harl Hill Scorchers; 'colors', 'the crown' and 'the herald' as local words for coat, Pressure and sensing; 'Who's king today?'; the Rootgate alder joke, which touches another writer's Moss Court realm.

calls.call: The style 'Kingdom of Nalūn' survives only in the salutation of its diplomatic instruments. The cities are free and no one has been crowned.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md and the 11-05 ruling say Nalūn is not a kingdom, but the Guild Accord page names 'the Kingdom of Nalūn' on the first circle. The old page already said the title exists because the Codex needs a sovereign signatory, so both hold without editing the Accord page.

calls.call: The High Chainlord and the Council of Links stay, as a signer with a chair and no crown and as a league council over seven city councils.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md says 'city councils, no crown'; the brief says to keep every old fact that still fits. The Powers page also relies on the Council of Links.

calls.call: Halcrest follows the book. The gauge-housings become assay posts, the brine and lift works are named without any draw, and the worked lamps stay costly.
calls.grounds: His order to stay true to the book, with BRIEF_REST retiring gauge-housings and the draw. The book's line about draw being too dear for the tea-house was rendered as worked lamps costing more than a sergeant's pay. The archived text still says draw and gauge-housing, so this is reported.

calls.call: The Cuttings run from the galleries under Halcrest out to Cutwall's moving face, and Orrel is a factor house holding galleries under Halcrest.
calls.grounds: The book places the Cuttings under Halcrest, and the old page makes Cutwall the district's chief city. Both are kept.

calls.call: The Ring is written as Marrowhold ('which older maps call the Ring'), and the Corridor now runs to its furnaces. Stannvaard is dropped from Nalūn's trade.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md: Stannvaard is gone, the Ring becomes Marrowhold, and Thornwall's corridor runs there. The Powers page and Inventory still name Stannvaard as Nalūn's credit partner and will need the same fix.

calls.call: The corridors were closed by the war that ended at Shimane, stated in the present. Cozbi Mahuo's name is dropped from this. The Alkia and Torven Greis passage and his quote stay.
calls.grounds: The book ends that war around 715, and Arc Two (Cozbi) is off public pages by the brief. The old page attributed the closure to a war with Cozbi.

calls.call: The Open Rulings block is removed from the public page, including the line naming Muken's mother as the bonded-labor test case and the Kōkan remnant. The tokenless underclass stays, with no named case.
calls.grounds: The task keeps the main cast's secrets off public pages. The book supports the drainage-book entries and the 'taken in' practice. The pending-ratification notes were process text.

calls.call: The Accord 'holds no territory' as a lawyer's truth. A pledged composite crown holds the land under the Sealed Charter, and the Accord holds the pledge and rules in fact.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md names the Guild Accord as who rules. The Articles page says it is not a sovereign and calls the Concord a composite monarchy. The Bench page gives land, law, levy, tax and hanging to the Crown. This reading keeps all of those.

calls.call: The Citadel stays a nexus between planes, and Sealhall is its foot on the ground: agents bound to the Lattice see the spire from there and the beacon line comes down there. The Neutral Chambers and the Bench's door are placed under the Ribs, and a Concord Gate in the forecourt.
calls.grounds: The Citadel page says it exists in no one realm, and KINGDOMS.md puts the court of judgment inside the bones. Sealhall therefore cannot be the Citadel. The Neutral Chambers had no fixed location on file.

calls.call: The Guild-hour water clock moves from Stannvaard to Sealhall, with the page noting that older rolls place it at Stannvaard.
calls.grounds: Stannvaard is gone as a state, and the brief says to move a fact that still fits. The Accord Inventory still says Stannvaard.

calls.call: The Articles' 'no standing army' and the Concord Legion are both kept, with the page openly noting the gap as a joke at the Accord's expense.
calls.grounds: This contradiction already exists between the Articles and the Military page. It is reported here and was not settled.

calls.call: Armies cross the Charter on a Writ by a named road, and most go around through the Midmarch.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md says the Center is marched through every generation, and Sealhall's law would not simply allow free passage. Both are kept.

calls.call: Verath is the Charter's pen town, with the Labor Authority's crossed hammer and chain seal and Darvo's line. The seal detail and the corridor crossing are taken from a scene in the pre-reset archive, while the quote and price are on the current Peoples page. Nothing else from that scene is used.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md lists Verath as a major place and says Beastkin law belongs here. The old scene is not canon for events, so only setting detail was taken and the exile plot was left out.

calls.call: The 'Brine crossing east to the marches of Sum-gol' stretch of the first circle is placed in the Midmarch, with several signing kings since deposed.
calls.grounds: The Accord page names that stretch and gives no realm for it. The Midmarch lies on that line and has no other Accord reach on file.

calls.call: Marrick arms on the Midmarch page are spears, and Han Do-yun's march is left undated so no date for Sum-gol's break-up is fixed.
calls.grounds: The task's rule on spears (R83-4), and the 11-05 ruling gives no year for the break-up.

calls.call: The empire appears only as one later-hand line on each page and Muken is not named. The Midmarch line ends on the clerk not recording what the empire did about being sold half a bridge.
calls.grounds: The task allows the device and keeps arc plot off these pages.

calls.call: Fox-Spirit people are mentioned only as on file, not at all on these pages, and the Bearkin hills beside the Charter are unnamed.
calls.grounds: The 11-05 ruling leaves the Fox-Spirit lineage pending Yoko Mishiro's card. Unnamed hills fix no new geography.

questions_for_isaac: Is the pledged 'Crown in Charter' the reading you want for the Concord, or should the Accord simply rule the Charter with no crown left there at all?
Should the Midmarch's river stay Aldwater, or does it already have a name in your head? The Painted Rivers and Kingsbridge pages will both lean on it.
The Whitlow Sixtoes story gives the Russet Crown its name by way of the 'nemo' window instruction. Keep it, or does the realm's writer need a different origin?

Sealhall's arena and Marrowhold are both built in giant bones. His art shows both, so the pages keep them unlinked and leave the beast disputed. Do you want them kept separate, or tied together later?

inventions: MANDATE: the she-wolf's name and rank, Kaan Shaarn, and the soldiers' saying 'Report to the wolf'.
MANDATE: Drekka Vreshen, 'Drekka Never-Late', Mandate-Holder in 715 IC.
MANDATE: the Grain Roll, the register of who counts as a member of the state. It replaces 'citizen' and 'citizenship'.
MANDATE: split ration-tallies, replacing military scrip.
MANDATE: a commander takes the district's name with the post. This explains how Vreth-Kaan is both a district and the commander in the 702 IC epigraph.
MANDATE: the Wall Games, and a joke that betting is unlawful by no decree because the Ironfold could not enforce one under the Assessment ratio.
MANDATE: the Door and the Knock, a named Lattice and Ironblood combo; a monthly list of officers commended.
MANDATE: a decree forbidding officers to own god-bone; a joint border moot at the foot of Marrowhold's ribs (the old Stannvaard commission moved).
MANDATE: the green smoke in the Kharven page's war row is attributed, by the wall's own guess, to Gorge copper burned with Isles brimstone.
ISLES: Khal-Serrat's gloss, with 'serrat' as an invented old root meaning the place where a weapon is set down.

ISLES: Voices (the delegates), the weapon racks at the foot of the Rock with an open-palm seating rite, the refused awning, the two-Voice hearth count every twelve years, the Speaker's spring recital of the law, sign-callers for Vow-keeping Voices, and the one-season War-Kaan.

ISLES: The Unpaid Toll, the Toll Entry read every spring, with the Scattering-era passes (the Ridgewall's ground) entered as surety; Greymane's yearly piece of slate sent in answer; no Isles brimstone or glass sold north of the wall.
ISLES: the Loans of Spears, including the Second Loan of four hundred in 688 IC.
ISLES: Mokk-Vesh the shipyard town; about four thousand Order spears in rotation; 'Deferred' as the Rock's heading on the slag-yards, raised eleven times.
ISLES: the c. -50 Last Lapse timeline row, and a row dating the Old Vaross page's axe-destroyed year 411 as 411 IC.
ISLES: the later-hand line that the moot found, by nine, that the debt passed to Whitemere.
ISLES: the jokes section.

calls.call: The Decree Stone is now as tall as a keep. The founding sentence runs high on it, and the old 12 ft by 8 ft surface is kept as the working face where decrees are cut.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md says 'a sentence carved in stone as tall as a keep' and wins over the old size. Splitting the Stone this way loses neither fact.

calls.call: The Ironfold is written as a sworn military order bound by the Crimson Order's Engraving, with no house or crown. 'Continental empire' is gone. The goblins' names 'Empire in the North', 'Imperium' and 'Imperator' stay only as bench slang.
calls.grounds: The task asks for a decree-state run by a military order. The Cold and The Debt use those slang names, and archived scenes stand.

calls.call: Tinker's Gorge keeps the old ~3,000 as the Roll figure, and adds 4,000 goblins a shift (8,000 in all) as uncounted contract hands. Those hands are paid in bunk space and soup and called 'the lesser' in decrees.
calls.grounds: The Debt (an archived scene) contradicts the page's 3,000, and scenes outrank wiki pages. The one explanation that keeps both numbers is that the Roll does not count contract hands.

calls.call: THE TEST: the Gorge as The Debt shows it is close to a factory, with shifts, quotas and a bell. I kept it, written as an Arsenal-style hand yard with no mains, gauges or draw-lamps. Lamp-wardens tend the lamps and the goods are valve-seats and bellows-fittings.
calls.grounds: Anything shown in an archived scene stays true (R82-46), and The Test names the Venetian Arsenal as a medieval model. This is the one item on these pages most exposed to The Test.

calls.call: Moved old district facts to the new map. Gorr-Shal now runs from the foot of the Greymane wall to Marrowhold's ribs, and Marrowkin factors replace Stannvaard's. Keth-Vorruk's settlers now come out of the Hundred Crowns of the Midmarch.
calls.grounds: Stannvaard is gone and the Ring became Marrowhold. KINGDOMS.md places neither border, and the old page has no district facing Kharven, so one had to be assigned.

calls.call: Ketsuen's relation moved to the Silver Cedars of Yukari, and the Thread Standard with it. The shared border is gone, so the two now deal only through observers.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md folds Ketsuen into the Silver Cedars, which lie in the South.

calls.call: Dawi replaced by Marrowkin throughout both pages, including the three oath-houses (now tally-houses) in the Scattering chart and the c. 500 IC contact. The Kuntur Reach Dwarves are dropped from the Isles page, so vent-forging is now taught by the Marrowkin.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md: 'The Dawi: replaced by the Marrowkin.' The Kuntur Reach still exists on the Dawi pages and the Reader's Codex. The volcanic-island kinship line was lost with the swap.

calls.call: Vesh-Undaal is the old tally name of the moot-isle, and Khal-Serrat is the name in use for both island and town.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md names Khal-Serrat the moot-isle. The Old Vaross page attests Vesh-Undaal, so the name is kept rather than erased.

calls.call: The parliament is now the Keth-Gorrum, a war-moot under open sky at the foot of the Rock. The opening story loses its slate roof, and the Tinkers' devices move to the cliff-top.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md: 'a war-moot under open sky'. The task also bans parliament wording. Its form draws on real open-air law assemblies: a law rock, a recited law, weapons brought to the moot.

calls.call: The Rock (High Concord script, Engraved) and the timber archive (Vaross tally-cuts) are both kept, as two records with different jobs. Sir Hamon's crest goes on the timber.
calls.grounds: The Expanse page and the Old Vaross page disagree about what the record is made of. Each stays true this way.

calls.call: Fixed internal date arithmetic. The '765th year' is now unbroken sitting since the c. -50 Last Lapse, 'fourteen hundred years' in The Orc Question became two thousand, 'early First Eon' became the long age before the Scattering, and the Ashenmoor Period is two centuries by the chroniclers and nearer twelve by the calendar.
calls.grounds: The charter at c. -1,050 and the Scattering at c. -1,340 cannot give 765 or 1,400 years by 715 IC. The Reader's Codex and the Geography hub quote the seven-hundred figures, so I kept 765 and explained it rather than changing it.

calls.call: Kept both etymologies of Undaar-Keth on the page: the heralds' reading (platform, open palm) and the grammarians' (standing thing, seal).
calls.grounds: The old page and the Old Vaross page disagree. The argument is left in the open and not settled.

calls.call: Placed the Fortress-Monastery of Haldrek and Echohold of Stoneblood Vale in the Mandate's Vreth-Kaan district.
calls.grounds: The Goblinoid Peoples page lists them as Crimson Order settlements with no location. The Isles page refers to 'mainland fortress-monasteries'.

calls.call: The Isles are the North's enemy through the old toll debt, the ridge passes claimed as goblinoid ground, a brimstone embargo, and loans of spears. The Mandate is the one fighting on the wall. The two stay cold to each other and agree only on this.
calls.grounds: Isaac's word that the hobgoblin states stay the North's enemy over the Greymane wall, built on the valley-lord and passes facts already in the Scattering. The present (715 IC) is a cold peace, and the nine-year war stays under the later hand.

calls.call: Kept the slag-yards under Gorr-Keth as a generic section on the Isles page, with no named person and no plot.
calls.grounds: They are in Vaashuuk's card and The Debt. The old page's clean picture of the Isles would have contradicted them.

calls.call: The old 'Flagged Gaps' heading stays. The out-of-world rows are removed or turned in-world, and the visual pass row is dropped because KINGDOMS.md now supplies the look.
calls.grounds: The brief says to keep headings, and these are public pages.

calls.call: The present-day Stone-Carver is left unnamed, with the page saying she has asked not to be named. The Fall and the Greymane gambit from The Uncounted stay off the page.
calls.grounds: Arc plot stays off public pages.

calls.call: Other pages still carry stale wording; I did not touch them: 'Old Vaross — The Goblinoid Tongue' (parliamentary wording, Stannvaard philologists, Dawi speakers), The Goblinoid Peoples (Dawi), A Reader's Codex and the Geography hub (parliament, Kuntur), The Powers of the Dark Ages (Stannvaard), Articles of the Accord (Stannvaard), and the Kharven page's relation row.
calls.grounds: Reported for the launching session to reconcile.

questions_for_isaac: Old Vaross and the Geography hub call the Isles' assembly a parliament. Should those pages move to 'war-moot' too? My pages assume yes.
Keep or cut the Toll Entry and the embargo as the Isles' reason for being the North's enemy? They are my invention, built on the valley-lords in the Scattering chart.
Is 8,000 uncounted goblins in Tinker's Gorge acceptable against a realm of about 55,000 on the Roll, or should The Debt's figure be read as loose?

inventions: Mosk-Vaal, people: Captain-General Piers Vantry, Dame Emmot Vantry, Mire-Mother Ssaaleth the Long Breath.

Mosk-Vaal, stories and places: the Third Column of the Aldwater League (683) and the Orchard, with Vantry pears planted on the dead in company order. Also the Second Battle of Rootgate. KINGDOMS only names Rootgate and Glowwater; their detail is mine.

Mosk-Vaal, offices and law: the Mire-Mother as an office, filled by a lung contest in Swamp Parun at Glowwater (the title is taken from the on-file move Mire-Mother's Yes). The Moss Court's words (We Will Keep It For You) and colors. The Salt Sentence and the salt licensing. The causeway and reclaiming fees. Debts passing to the tree. Nine-year grown rooms.

Mosk-Vaal, words and trade: the meaning of the name Mosk-Vaal. Trade in moss-dye, moth silk, wound molds and lamp-stalks. Aura coat 'ssuul, the rind'; Pressure 'the damp'; sensing 'asking the moss'. Moths and Selunite as the source of the forest's light.

Rose Coils, people: Marshal Corbel Aumery, Captain Ysolde Penhale, Remembrancer Zsovrath Oda-riss, Gorvaine the Unanswered (the conqueror on the statue, supplying a name for Natalie's reading in KINGDOMS.md).

Rose Coils, stories and places: the War of the Rose Teeth (697) and the poison Widow's Rose. Bothhands, the hospital town at the ford. Lamp Stair. The fused-glass account of Stoneglass Hollow, with past events showing in the glass. The Reading of Gorvaine.

Rose Coils, institutions and words: the Standing Record and the Remembrancer. Words (It Has Been Tried) and colors. The posted-price trade in physic, poison and memory. A bed paid for with a true story. Aura coat 'the entry'; Pressure 'the objection'; sensing 'looking him up'. The land as curved rose ridges.
Violet Peaks, people: King Odo Gambrel of Upper Marl, Warden Vessaly Caelward, called Nobody's Landing.

Violet Peaks, schools and contests: the King's Hat and the Long Step match. The Gray Kites, Highroost Shrikes, Stair Wardens, Longdrop Swifts, Old Mews and Lilac Stair. The moves Highroost Stoop and Long Afternoon. Words (Step Off) and colors.
Violet Peaks, law and trade: the hoisters' company, the Drop court, fowlers and the bridge penalty, the feather-fletching and almanac trades. Aura coat 'the lift'; Pressure 'the downdraft'.

Avian Kin anatomy: crests, forearm vanes, and flight as an earned art. The Guild's rolls carried only one table row on the Avian Kin. The summit pool as a Cymorath Core (the Wellspring itself is on file; the site is new).
Russet Crown, people: Assessor Pell Wickham, Queen Sefa Tuen-zhiv.

Russet Crown, story and places: the Roll of 668, in which every resident gave the name 'nobody', and its legal effect. The Heap's history and the rite of arrival. The Underhill Forge, as descendants of Orsa Underhill. Lower Sedge. The Long Way, the runaway road. Collar-bits as local money.
Russet Crown, law and words: the ban on keeping lists. Rent as one day in seven. 'Licensed returners'. Pressure 'the old man'; sensing 'smelling the iron'.

Central Warlords page: Quartermaster-General Wat Hasketh and the four bills of 709, the Table Nobody Called (Bothhands, 612), the central rule, and the wants table. Also the 'new king has sent inquiries' line and the later-hand margin notes on Whitemere across all five pages.

calls.call: Placed old beastkin settlements inside the Russet Crown beyond KINGDOMS.md's list: Greyfang Crossing, the Shrine of Nine Howls, the Glade of the Slumbering Root. Lumis Village, Korr Orvun and Ulg-Vorakar stay unplaced. The Dusk Quarter of Altherion stays in Altherion.
calls.grounds: Keep every old fact and move it to where it now belongs. Those three had no fixed location on file, and the Crown needs Wolfkin and Bearkin seats. Only Catkin towns are listed in KINGDOMS.md.

calls.call: Placed the three Verdant settlements on file (Ghurash Hollow, the Blooming Mire, Totemdeep) in the Moonlight Forest, alongside KINGDOMS.md's three.
calls.grounds: They are the Verdant settlements the Goblinoid page names, and the old Expanse page says the bands went into interior wetlands.

calls.call: Moved the Dawi relations on the beastkin pages to the Marrowkin: Bearkin 'honor-bound kinship' with the Ember Holds, and Serpentkin 'mutual respect grounded in preservation', now applied to the Marrowkin tally.
calls.grounds: The Marrowkin replace the Dawi. The source pages still say Dawi and need their own pass.

calls.call: Assigned Cymorath as the Wellspring of the Caelspire summit pool. The Avian Kin essence stays on the page as 'Aer and Caelum', as the table gives it.
calls.grounds: Cymorath is the canon Air of Ascent (freedom and motion). Only the site is invented. The Sixty are untouched.

calls.call: Left the great tree of Mosk-Vaal and the permanent autumn of the Russet Forest as disputed among scholars, with no Archon or Titan named. The Caelspire bridge is only attributed by Measurewrights to the Great Spirit War.
calls.grounds: The instruction not to invent or kill any Archon or Titan, and R83-11.

calls.call: Kept the Marrick company's spears as spears. They appear in the Vantry story as a walk-out at contract's end, reusing the habit on the Southern Warlords page.
calls.grounds: R83-4 keeps pike for the Imperial Age, and the Southern page already has spears.

calls.call: Aligned with sibling staged pages. Tollgarth and Pennycrown are used as the Hundred Crowns page defines them, so the two armies became an invented Aldwater League and Odo became king of Upper Marl, crowned at Pennycrown. The Vantry suit went to the Harrowgate Fair Court. Sealhall took the lawyers because Waxgate is the wax town. Enforcement's collectors still go into the Russet Forest, matching the Charter page.
calls.grounds: Those pages landed while I wrote. Their facts win where they are specific.

calls.call: Left Elves and Fox-Spirits off these pages entirely, including Elven relations listed for Wolfkin and Serpentkin (the First Betrayal, scholarly cooperation). Saiya of the Catkin record is also left out.
calls.grounds: Task instruction on Elves and Fox-Spirits. Saiya is a working mercenary and needs no place on a public realm page.

calls.call: Used the later-hand margin device on all five pages for Whitemere, with comic and procedural content only: no battles, no Muken by name, nothing on the split. The Central page carries a short in-world 'On the record' block in the archivist's voice, in place of the Southern page's process notes.
calls.grounds: The 715 present, the task's allowance, and arc plot staying off public pages. The memory rule keeps him and the process off pages.

questions_for_isaac: The Five Beastkin Lineages page and others still say Dawi for the relations I moved to the Marrowkin. Those source pages need the swap at merge, or the two will read differently.
KINGDOMS.md has a stray empty table header at line 31-32, above the Central Warlords note. It is harmless; I read the second table as the law.
Nothing is struck or blocked. Every name above is yours to keep or cut, the Avian Kin anatomy and the 668 'nobody' roll most of all, since they carry the most weight.

inventions: PEOPLE, pitched for his red pen: chest high to a human, door wide, twice the weight they look, cannot swim. Large wide-set eyes, amber to coal red, with a reflective back layer; carved horn or ivory slit visors in daylight, by clan.
Hot rust-dark blood that glows dull in a dark cut, snow melting on them, steam in the cold, and cold-sickness after a long winter away from the Ring.
The rise: ivory bone ridges through the skin from about age thirty, both sexes, with Soul-Runes cut into them. Skin grained like old tusk. Beards on both sexes, ash-white yellowing to rib color.
Deepkin as the people's cold version: slag-gray eyes, chalk rise, no heat.
Sound: a low flat voice with an under-note felt in the breastbone; bone-hearing with the jaw to a wall; rib-knock, a tapped code that carries the strong grade as a doubled knock.

NAMING: given name (Body element plus work element), oath-name in second place, line in the genitive, and the cut-name, the largest thing you ever took from the Body (Sixty Tuns, Half a Rib, Thimble). Childhood shift-names such as Second-Shift Four. The First Entry around age seven, with a smear of marrow on bread entered as the opening debt.

TONGUE: Tallukieli (Tally-Tongue), Ytinkreis (their own name), Luuthruk (Marrowhold), rintaluu, solisluu, kylki, Ykt-kaht Kylki (Twelfth Rib), luu, ytin, veri, hehkuveri (glow-blood), hiillos, Lainur (the Lender), velka, palaute. The Return Clause line 'Lainuran palaute on'. Out-Tally and Low Tally as register and dialect names. 'High Line' and 'Cask Line' for the old High Dwarves and Barrel Dwarves.

DEBT: the Return Clause on every sale, the Cutting Right (an unentered cut is tried like murder), bone-runners, the dead 'returned' as payment against the account, rolls read with their balance on the Drawing-Off.
The Lean: sold pieces are reputed to lean toward the Ring, left disputed between Guild assayers and Measurewrights.
GOODS: old ivory, sinew, marrow-tallow, bloodslag, ember dye and relics. Emberwort (the red growth, moss to forty-foot fern) and redcaps (its fungus).

PLACES: the Cutting Fair at Collarbone; Breastbone citadel above with Thane-Gorr's seven levels below; Collarbone as the market bone; the Twelfth Rib housing Kegshard Hold; Kolmthruk on the Third Rib and Barkstone on the northern wall as the rest of the Upper Ring; the Seat as the high ground at Altherion.

PEOPLE AND STORIES: King Hobart of Pennycrown and the leaning throne (651 to 662 IC); hold-clerk Vappu Tarrekk Ollan, called Thimble; Council Chair Mirja Hiilekk Solisan, called Sixty Tuns; Ilmo Torvekk Kreisan as the grammar's sample name.

STREET AND WAR: rent by warmth, rib-sounders, the First Shift Reds and Third Shift Coals, Worked Ground as the Forge Guard's named move, red-enameled rib-ivory shields, the jokes on the realm page, and the new swears Bone-thief and The Lender's looking.
A dispute planted on the realm page: the Accord has never produced a receipt for the bones at Sealhall, and the Tally says they are not in it.

calls.call: 'Dawi' and 'Guild Seat of Stannvaard' survive only as older names on old rolls and in songs, and no state of that name stands.
calls.grounds: 43 archived scene files say Dawi and are not rewritten here. R82-46 keeps what scenes show as true. This lets the replacement stand without breaking them. Overturnable.

calls.call: Scene-facing facts were kept: short stature, beards, soul-runes, forge-flush, Thane-Gorr, Kolmthruk, Kegshard, Barkstone, the Seat, oath-name second, doer at the front, Tally slot at the back.
calls.grounds: The Weak Grade, The Revolution of the Inner World and the Kujo-arc scene depend on them. The alterations were added on top of these facts rather than replacing them.

calls.call: Breastbone is the capital and Thane-Gorr is the name of the seven forge levels under it.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md and the task set Breastbone as capital; scenes and the petition story need Thane-Gorr. The citadel follows the art: pale spires, thin bridges, a domed hall, round terraced halls, a low town, everything else ember red.

calls.call: Altherion, the River Crown, the Grand Church and the Ember Magistrates stay inside Marrowhold on the northern rim.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS.md is silent on them and the Sancta Lux pages seat the Church at Altherion, so the old fact still fits. The water clock and the Guild hour move to the Seat at Altherion, which keeps the Weak Grade's rainy Seat.

calls.call: What died is left undecided on every page, and Varūn the Deepwright is kept as the maker and teacher they swear by, with the holds refusing to say what he and the Body have to do with each other.
calls.grounds: The rule is to invent or kill no Archon or Titan. Varūn is called a Titan on the Dawi pages but is not among the Fourteen, so I made no claim either way. See questions.

calls.call: The deep halls are read as the oldest galleries under the basin floor; the people's Tally puts them inside the Body from the first entry; the Fractures and the eight branches carry over unchanged.
calls.grounds: The fall sits in the Great Spirit War, which the Guild keeps off the count, and the Fractures are Second and Third Eon. This keeps every date, figure and Wellspring row while leaving the entry date disputed through the Errata.

calls.call: All numbers, Soul Paths, Wellspring rows and risk figures for the High Line, Cask Line and Deepkin were carried word for word; only the lineage names changed.
calls.grounds: BRIEF_REST rule that nothing is lost.

calls.grounds: The old page put the graded name in first place in those samples, against its own rule and against the Weak Grade ('the oath-name sits in the second place').

questions_for_isaac: Do you keep the Marrowkin look (hot eyes and slit visors, rust-glow blood, the rise, both-sex beards, sinks like an anvil, under-note and bone-hearing) and the cut-name naming culture? This is the pitch you asked for, and the default if you say nothing.
Do you accept 'Dawi' as the old name of the same people, so archived scenes still read true? The other option is a clean break, where those scenes become old lore.

Varūn the Deepwright is called a Titan on the Dawi pages but is not among the Fourteen, and the Old World still has a kingdom of Varūn with its own dwarves. I left all of it open. Should Varūn stay, and should those Old World dwarves remain dwarves?

The five Reach branches (Kuntur Reach, Tallow Clans, Windward Herds, Tower-Kin, Passwardens) are written as Marrowkin severed from the Body and cooling off, and their page still reads The Reach Dwarves. Do they stay on those terms, and should that page be rewritten next?
Borin Ironheart appears in 12 scenes and has no card, and Nella Forgeman's scenes were not checked. Should Borin read as Marrowkin from here on, and does he get a cut-name?

inventions: Sum-gol's fall: the last Calling on the first day of autumn 602 IC; Emperor Rokju Mahuo; the doubled salt tax; the Balcony of Answers and Palace of Answers; the Baengnok (the White Stag, reading the art's pale antlered device as a bound power of the line, explicitly no Archon or Titan) walking out by the East Gate; the empire's three-hundred-year span; tribute by house (records, spearmen, water, horses, fleet, one crow a year); the Mahou as kings of Sum-gol only for about three generations after 602, which fits the existing '661, when the Mahou kings still sat at Sum-gol'.

Sum-gol present: the yearly Calling still read to a crowd with an elder of the Yan reciting and a letter from the Ryu; a city of about 15,000 (the old Ketsuen province figure) in streets built for 150,000; domes stripped on the north faces; Post-House in the imperial mews; cinnabar and dye works at Cheolsan; stilt town and linen-wrapped rakers at Yeomjeon; Post law (the sacred bag); street foods; scavenger crews.

Holy Sea: the Sounding Walk's mechanism (barefoot oath, dark wet footprints till sundown, assay fork reads depth, dry stone for a false oath, what it cannot do), and the slang 'dry-footed'; the opening story of Tobit Gurnard, Gaspard Vauquelin, his brother the Archdeacon of Rimward and the galley Good Intent (683); Palatine Aurélien Cassard, nearly blind; the Stair of Testimony (1,100 steps); Bridge of Notaries (the art's arched bridge); the Lone Clerk (the art's watchtower); Laundry Steps; Whites and Inks bracket schools; foot-washers; population 60,000; benches pairing a cleric with a Lambert; crossbow companies on the Stair.

Jade Plains: Lucky Bao and Rain-on-Slate (694); Yan horses that come home when their name is read; Elder Yan Shouyi's age (ninety) and morning ride; Elders of Stables, Ledgers, Remounts and Tablets; the Emperor's stall entered as 'held'; Lantern Fair; Qingyuan population 40,000; Yuquan river jade; Mashi as a nine-week tent market; bracket schools Silver Bridles, Black Girths, Yuquan Waders; why northerners say Grey and the Yan say Jade.

Copper Coast: Lantern Night 671 with warden captain Gim Dol-soe, old Deok-sun the net-widow and Admiral-Lord Ryu Seok-ju, as the origin of the lanterns; the reef called the Sawbacks; the books headed 'held for the Throne'; Ryu Ha-eun's age (53) and looks; Haeseong population 70,000; Long Mole, Salt Quay; Geumpo's character and Guild of Pilots; the Tide Court and harbor-mothers; wreck-right and ship's cats; toll-forts every thirty miles; Green Tide, Geumpo Gilders, Bad Weather; hill copper workings behind the coast.

Silver Cedars: Karasuyama's rookery and crow-wards; Sugidani's sawpits, bark paper and tea; Senri's Gate as the town at the standing stones; Long Water, Reedgate, Maren Ottertail and the other moved Ketsuen material stays as filed; the Marrowkin community in the Lake Districts, replacing the Dawi one; the Marrowkin-Yukari grudge line; the carvers joke.

Sapphire Wells: the Blue Morning of 647 with Annis Blewitt and Warden Odo Corwen, as the origin of kingfisher blue and the Dyers' exception; 'blue to the elbow'; Maud's brass crown in a box; blue-coated keepers with brass keys; Brightwater population 25,000; Cask Yards, Lease Court; Hotwell's raft ring and Kingfisher Steps' 31 tiers; Blue Bracket with Dyers, Coopers and Dregs; closing Cores on an enemy as the house's way of war; 'After you, Maud.'

Ochre Fields: the Broken Cart at the ford (the art's broken cart) with Dob Harkness, Big Marget Marrick, the hiring fair of 631 and the battle of Sorley Bridge; the clause 'as long as the cart stands'; Guild of Wrights resetting the break; Hammerford population 50,000; Hiring Hall, Moot and Moot Law at Pikemoot; Musterfield's sixteen-deep drill; rent paid in children to the muster; the Widows' Chest; companies the Late Arrivals, Stubble Boys, Mother Hallam's Own, Sixth Blacks; the drill for a high-Stage fighter; blister-wives; Gerrit losing his ear to a Tenrai on his own side.
Geography: the Jade Plains with the Wellheads west and the iron hills east; Karasuyama above the Enclave; Sallowgate on a western branch of the salt road.
Later-hand lines on the Whitemere empire (Holy Sea, Sapphire Wells, Ochre Fields, Southern Warlords), in general terms only.

calls.call: 'Attestis', the Holy Sea's Wellspring on the old Ketsuen page, is treated as the Court's Latin name for the Aether under the shelf, on no Guild list of the Sixty, with the Thaloré reading as the most respected account. The Sōhai claim that it is a Moto scar is reported as their claim.
calls.grounds: The word appears only on the Ketsuen page and is absent from the Sixty; the Long Reading gives the Thaloré reading; the Sixty are fixed (R79-11). Nothing was added to the Sixty.

calls.call: Marrick arms are spears throughout. KINGDOMS' 'pikes in the thousands' became long ash spears. The place name Pikemoot and the title Captain of the Long Pike stay, explained as Fields usage for any long ash spear. The Warlords page's 'far end of a pike' became spear.
calls.grounds: The task's reading of R83-4, against KINGDOMS' names, which I kept as written.

calls.call: Ketsuen's Cedar Enclave versus Senri's Gate: the Enclave stays the house seat on its hill, and Senri's Gate becomes the town at the standing stones and capital of the Reach, holding the Council, Academy and Archive of Provings. The Yukari Inventory's 'old Enclave is Senri's Gate now' reads as a mistake of older books.
calls.grounds: KINGDOMS names the Cedar Enclave as the major place; the Bloodline page and Naiser's card make it the living seat; Ketsuen's facts still needed a home.

calls.call: The Reach keeps its Council of Threads, Crow's Seat, Proving, Thread Standard, Thread Guard and provinces as a land under House Yukari at arm's length. With Sum-gol removed there are seven Thread-Wardens, and population falls from 95,000 to 80,000 (the sum of the remaining rows). Race percentages became rough fractions because Mahuo and Dawi moved.
calls.grounds: Task: fold in what fits; KINGDOMS: Ketsuen is gone as a state; Sum-gol is sovereign southern ground by the 11-05 rulings.

calls.call: Niran Yukari stays on the public page as the boy carver of the Reach's founding and designer of the Crow's Seat, with no age or later arc. Left off: the Septarch transition, the Seven Crows, Dhaerin's death, the old Kharven and Sodoku relation lines and Sum-gol's negotiated incorporation.
calls.grounds: Main-cast secrets and arc plot stay off public pages. The Inventory ties Dhaerin's death to a sealed rite. Naiser's card notes the Naiser and Niran kinship is unrecorded, so the page does not state it.

calls.call: Cozbi on the page is limited to his title, age, renown lines, public refusal of crown and vermilion, olive coat, the stated want (the Order, the Keepers), priced passage work, his voice line and 'fights the way he gives a dinner'. Left off: stats and kit, what he does with letters, who pays the couriers, the seam, his dead, soul harvest, Hiromi and the past-tense tell.
calls.grounds: Task: only what his card makes public; the card's 'Notes (sealed)' section and 'desire underneath' stay off. The 'by his own hand' line about the vermilion is on the card outside the sealed notes, so it is framed as a dinner-table boast.

calls.call: The Ryu 'still answer to the name' and also stopped forwarding the money; both are kept as one joke, the separate books headed 'held for the Throne'. The Yan answer by reciting titles and keep a held stall.
calls.grounds: Rulings say they belong to the Dynasty; the existing page has the Ryu keeping the revenue. Both facts had to stand.

calls.call: The Warlords line 'The seven have never had a king' became 'no emperor since 602', and 'beyond any crown' became 'beyond any living crown'. The Mahuo section's 'as kings' now reads emperors until 602, then kings. The public 'seated by Isaac's ruling' phrase was reworded, and the page's existing 'On the record' block was kept with one added 11-05 line.
calls.grounds: Isaac's 2026-11-05 word that Sum-gol was the empire of the South. All other facts on that page stand.

calls.call: Rimward stays two towns: the Sea's harbor at the bay's western arm and a free city of Nalūn.
calls.grounds: The old Nalūn page already says 'Not the Holy Sea of Alabaster's harbor of the same name'; KINGDOMS lists both.

calls.call: Grey Plain, Wellheads, Long Fields, Thousand Moorings and Yukari valleys stay as regional and map names inside the new realm names.
calls.grounds: They carry scenes and cards (Léonard's father died on the Grey Plain); KINGDOMS only names the realms. The Jade Plains page gives a reason for both names.

calls.call: The words 'bank' and 'banking' are avoided: deposit-and-lending and money-keepers instead. Lamp-wardens at Haeseong are Wellhead men; wikilinks go only to my seven pages and existing wiki pages, and other realms are named in plain text.
calls.grounds: R83-4 puts banks in the Imperial Age. Other agents' filenames were not known when I wrote.

questions_for_isaac: The art for Sum-gol reads as old glory, so I wrote the present city as still gold and bright but stripped and nine-tenths empty, at about 15,000 people. Is that the Sum-gol you want in 715, or should it be fuller?
The Baengnok, a great bound White Stag that walked out at the fall, is my reading of the art's pale antlered device. Keep it, or should the device be only heraldry?
The Walk's dark footprints are my invented mechanism for how the Sea weighs an oath. It decides many future court scenes, so strike it now if it is wrong.
Pikemoot and Captain of the Long Pike keep the word 'pike' as a Fields word for a long spear. Would you rather rename both, say to Spearmoot and Captain of the Long Ash?

calls.call: The state of Kharven in 715 is taken from The Uncounted: the Tenrai have held the rock for 300 years, the red chair has been empty for 40, the forty-year war has just ended, and the Hall of Verdicts and the old summons law hold the houses. calls.grounds: Archived scenes (rung 4) outrank wiki pages (rung 6). The 'no oath running, so summons law' reading is my own bridge between the old page's oath law and The Iron Fist of the Keld.

calls.call: Ulf Stark is Lord of Hollenmark in 715 and Zaehaerys Stark moves to the later hand. The 'ancestor at the boundary stones' became 'the Lord of Hollenmark'.
calls.grounds: Ulf's card and Chapter Three outrank the old page, and a note on Chapter Eight places Zaehaerys in Hild Ice's era. Factions at a Glance still names Zaehaerys and needs the same fix.

calls.call: Old page timeline fixes: Greymane and Hallenfeld already hold their posts before Muken, who confirms them; Stark, Greymane, Ashmore, Thornwall, Keld and Hallenfeld bindings are all later hand; the page gains a 'How the years run' section. I gave no year for his crown beyond 'within a few winters', and kept the old sixteen years as 'by the usual count'.
calls.grounds: Task direction, plus Muken being about 16 in 715. His card (18, six months after the Great War of the North) implies a crown near 717, and adding sixteen years puts the end of the reign before the split at about 740, so it fits. No date is printed.

calls.call: The old Kharven table had Thornwall, Ashmore and Hallenfeld 'conquered in the traditional sense'. Dropped in favor of stone (Ashmore), a price (Thornwall, free of the Ore Council) and appointment and paper (Hallenfeld). 'Muken always stopped' is kept. The Keld page and Banner page record both accounts of how the Keld were won: three days at the fires and the predator, and a battle on the ice first.
calls.grounds: Edric's and Hisae's cards and Chapters Eighteen and Nineteen outrank the old table. Both Keld accounts are kept openly, without narrating the Skeldmere. Later scene plot and the name Aksel Keld are left off.
